title: 𓂋𓄿 𓏌𓅱 𓉐𓂋𓏏𓂻 𓅓 𓉔𓂋𓅱𓇳
titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 3
part: Spell 17, part 3 — the Eye of Ra, the lords of Maat and the seven spirits (Plates 8–10)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates VIII, IX, X. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 36–41; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: The third part of Spell 17 goes on with the commentary: the Eye of Ra in its rage is healed by Thoth, and Ra is born from Mehet-weret, the Great Flood. Ani then greets the lords of Maat and the tribunal behind Osiris and asks them to drive out his evil as they did for the seven spirits, and the glosses name the four sons of Horus, the seven spirits and the chief of the tribunal. On the papyrus it runs from Plate 8, line 70, to Plate 10, line 109, from the question on the hair raised at the time of the storm to the statement 'I am his ba in the midst of the Two Tjafi', which the next part explains.

sentences.i: It is the right Eye of Ra in its raging against him after he had sent it out.
sentences.n: irt 'the Eye' is the eye ir with t and a stroke. imnt 'right' is the emblem of the West (R14), which also writes imn 'right', with m as complement, the feminine ending t and, as classifier, a cord with a loop at its end (coded V12, approximate; the sign is not clear in the print): the feminine of imny 'right', agreeing with irt (Budge: àmt). n 'of' is not made feminine. nšny·s 'its raging' is nšny, the word for the storm at the end of part 2 (its pool š a box with strokes, approximate), with the bolt ·s, 'its', the Eye's. r·f 'against him' is the mouth r and the viper ·f with its horns. m-ḫt 'after', as in part 2. hꜣb·f 'he sent' is the courtyard h, ꜣ, the foot b, two strokes and walking legs, with ·f: hꜣb 'send', a sḏm·f after m-ḫt, 'after he had sent'; the strokes are not read, and Budge's numeral 72 is printed inside the word (Budge: habi-f, 'he hath made it to depart'). sw 'it' is the dependent pronoun, the object; the Eye is feminine, but sw is written. Ra sent his Eye out against his enemies, and in its fury it turned on him.

sentences.i: It was Thoth who raised the hair from it; he has brought it, living, sound and healthy, without harm(?), to its lord.
sentences.n: in with a noun and a participle singles out the doer: in ḏḥwty ṯs 'it was Thoth who raised'. in is the reed with a sign that is not clear in the print (coded W25, approximate; Budge: àn). ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t, two strokes and a god. ṯs is the tethering rope ṯ and the bolt s with a forked post (coded U39, approximate) and the low sign U15 as classifiers: the participle of ṯs 'raise' (Budge: θes). šn 'the hair' is the cord šn (V7) with n, two strokes and a lock of hair. im is the adverb 'there, therein', here 'from it'. in·n·f 'he has brought' is the jar on legs in (W25, approximate) with n, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·f. The bolt after it, printed after Budge's numeral 73, is split off here as the dependent pronoun s 'it', the Eye. The water n that follows has no clear place and is not translated. ꜥnḫ wḏꜣ snb 'living, sound, healthy' is written short, as after a king's name: the sign of life, the tall sign ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) for wḏꜣ and the folded cloth for snb. n bgꜣ is the arms of negation, then the foot b, the jar-stand g (approximate), ꜣ and the bird of bad things: bgꜣ is taken from its classifier as 'harm, failing', perhaps a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack' with the ꜣ after g (Budge: beḳa, 'defect'); the word is doubtful. n nb 'to its lord', Ra; no suffix is written, and 'its' is supplied. Thoth, the healer, brings the Eye back whole.

sentences.i: Another saying: it is the Eye when it was ill, when it was weeping for its fellow.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. wnn is the hare wn with n twice, the verb 'be' in its doubled stem; with irt pw after it, it is taken as opening the statement and is not translated apart (Budge: unen, 'it is'). m mr·s 'in its being ill' is the hoe mr (coded U6, approximate; the print shows a stick with a small cup at its top) with m and r as complements, the bird of bad things and ·s: the infinitive of mr 'be ill' with a suffix (Budge: mer-s, 'it is sick'). m wnn·s ḥr rmi 'when it was weeping': wnn·s, with Budge's numeral 74 printed before it, is the infinitive of wnn after m, with ·s as its subject; with ḥr and an infinitive after it, it makes the progressive, 'it was weeping'. rmi 'weep' is r and m, two reeds and the weeping eye (D9). sn·f 'its fellow' is printed as two short strokes over a small pot (coded Z4 and W24, approximate): taken as the type's form of the arrowhead sn, with the pot for its n, and ·f with its horns (Budge: sen-f). The fellow of the one eye of the sky is the other: the sun and the moon.

sentences.i: Then Thoth stood up to spit on it.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes psꜣgs, with a second s (Budge's 'sic'); read psg. ꜥḥꜥ is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with ꜥ and walking legs: taken as the infinitive 'standing up', with in ḏḥwty 'by Thoth' naming the doer, as in ḏd in N 'said by N' (Budge: āḥā àref àn Teḥuti, 'standeth up then Thoth'). irf 'then' is the reed, r and the viper with its horns. ḏḥwty is written here without the god. r psg 'to spit' is r with the infinitive: the stool p, the bolt s, ꜣ (not read) and the jar-stand g, then, after Budge's numeral 75, the second bolt, a curved stem with bristles and a cross-bar at its tip that cannot be identified (coded M3, approximate), and the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of what the mouth does. Budge reads pesaḳ, 'wash', and prints -nes with it as one word; here n·s, water n and the bolt, is split off as the preposition with ·s, 'on it', the Eye. The reading psg is likely but not sure. Spittle was a remedy in Egyptian healing, and Thoth is the healer of the Eye.

sentences.l: (iw) · have-seen-I · Ra · born · in · yesterday · at · the-hindquarters(?) · of · Mehet-weret
sentences.i: I have seen Ra, born yesterday from the hindquarters(?) of Mehet-weret.
sentences.n: A new statement; iw opens it. mꜣꜣ·n·i 'I have seen' is the eye with the sickle mꜣ printed beneath it, the vulture ꜣ twice, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i, here the man raising one arm. ms 'born' is the three skins ms with s and the woman giving birth (B3): the passive participle of msi. m sf 'yesterday' is the folded cloth s and the viper f with its horns, with the sun as classifier, as in part 1. r is 'at, towards'; the sense asks for 'from'. ḫpdt is the placenta ḫ, p, the hand d and t, with a fish with a hatched fin (coded K1, approximate) and two small loops (coded V1, approximate) as classifiers that cannot be identified; the reading and the sense 'hindquarters' follow Budge's χepṭet and are not sure. mḥt-wrt 'Mehet-weret', 'the Great Flood', is the crown of the north mḥ with water, the swallow wr with r and t, and a recumbent cow with an object on its back (coded E1, approximate) and a cobra as classifiers; the t of mḥt is not written (Budge: Meḥ-urt). Mehet-weret is the sky as a cow in the waters, who gives birth to the sun.

sentences.i: His soundness is my soundness, and the other way round.
sentences.n: wḏꜣ·f 'his soundness' is the chick w, the tall sign ḏꜣ (U28, approximate), ꜣ and the roll, with ·f: the noun from wḏꜣ 'be sound'. A noun set beside a noun is a sentence without a verb: 'his soundness is my soundness'. wḏꜣ·i has ·i, the man raising one arm. Budge's two groups θes and rer are joined here as ṯs-pẖr 'and vice versa', the phrase that says a statement also holds the other way: a knotted cord (coded S24, approximate) for ṯs, and an oval loop (coded V10, approximate) for pẖr, whose sign, the coiled intestine, the type may draw so; Budge renders 'conversely'. How the phrase is built is not sure: ṯs is also the word for a saying, and pẖr is 'turn round'. 'He' is Ra, born in the line before: the dead man is well when the sun is well, and the sun when he is.

sentences.n: ḏdw 'is said' is a tall tapering sign standing for ḏ (U28, approximate, as in part 1), the hand d and the chick w, with the man with hand to mouth and a stroke: the passive sḏm of ḏd, with the w it sometimes has (Budge: t'eṭu, 'Spoken'). ḥr tp·f is literally 'upon his head': the face ḥr and the head tp, each with its stroke, and ·f. The papyrus writes ir ẖrt ꜣḫw ipw 7 in red, with the numeral after ipw here (in lines 86 and 102 it comes before it); ipw has a single stroke, and Budge's numeral 99 is printed inside it. 'They are' is supplied. sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd ir ꜣḫw 7 ipw in red; ipw has the coil w, and Budge's numeral 103 follows it. The seven names run on into the next unit; they are left as names, their sense not clear. nḏḥ-nḏḥ is water n, a cobra-like sign for ḏ (I10, approximate) and the wick ḥ, written twice, with a god (Budge: Net'eḥ-net'eḥ). iꜣqd-qd is the reed and ꜣ, then a tall wedge (coded Aa28, approximate) for qd with d and a pot, which is not read, written twice, with a god (Budge: Àaqeṭqeṭ). The third name begins with a sign that cannot be identified (coded V26, approximate; Budge: àn), then rdi (r and the giving arm), n·f, b with a flame (coded Q7, approximate) for bs 'flame' and f, ḫnty 'foremost', the shelter h twice with the flame for hh 'heat'(?) and f with a god: perhaps 'who … his flame, foremost of his heat'; Budge's numeral 104 is printed before its last viper. ꜥq-ḥr-imy-wnwt-f is a long-necked bird (coded G35, approximate) for ꜥq 'enter' with q and walking legs, ḥr 'face', imy 'who is in' and wnwt 'hour' with the star and the sun, and f with a god (Budge: Aq-ḥer-àmmi-unnut-f). All these readings are doubtful.

sentences.i: As for that day of 'Come, then, there!', it is the saying of Osiris to Ra: 'Come, then, there!'
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ẖrt hrw pf mi ir·k im in red. pf 'that' is the stool p and the viper f: the masculine demonstrative, after its noun. No n is written before mi here. mi 'come!' is the owl lying over the arm, i, two strokes and walking legs, as in line 88. ḏd wsir pw n rꜥ: ḏd, the cobra over the hand, is the infinitive 'saying', with wsir after it as a direct genitive, 'the saying of Osiris', and n rꜥ 'to Ra', the god alone. Budge renders 'the saying to Osiris by Ra'; but n does not name a doer, and the grammar makes Osiris the speaker. Budge's numeral 109 is printed inside the second ir·k. The god of the dead calls the sun to the meeting of the two in the world below.

sentences.l: is-seen(?) · is-assigned(?) · seat-my · to · the-West
sentences.i: It is seen(?) that my seat is assigned(?) in the West.
sentences.n: This line is doubtful. mꜣꜣ·tw is the sickle mꜣ with the eye, ꜣ twice, t and w: mꜣꜣ 'see' with the passive tw, 'one sees, it is seen' (Budge: maa-tu, 'see'). The next group, which Budge leaves without transliteration, is the horned viper with its × crossed by a stick ending in a hanging loop (coded V25, approximate). It is taken, doubtfully, as the sign wḏ 'command, assign', with the viper not read: wḏ is often written with the cobra ḏ as its complement, and the snake joined to the stick may be that cobra drawn as the viper. wḏ is taken as a passive sḏm, 'is assigned', with st·i as its subject; Budge's English 'decreed is it' may rest on the same guess. st·i 'my seat' joins Budge's set and à: the bolt and t, writing st 'seat', with ·i, the man raising one arm. st 'seat' usually has the seat sign; bolt and t alone is the usual spelling of the dependent pronoun st 'it', and Budge reads it so, with the man as 'for me' ('decreed is it for me'). r imntt 'to the West', the emblem of the West with t twice and the desert hills. wḏ r 'assign to' is the verb used in part 1 of Osiris assigned to Set-Imentet.

sentences.l: I · ba-his · who-is-in-the-midst-of · the-Two-Tjafi(?)
sentences.i: I am his ba, who is in the midst of the Two Tjafi(?).
sentences.n: A new statement. ink 'I' is the pot in and the basket k, without a seated figure. bꜣ·f 'his ba' is the jabiru bꜣ with the bowl and flame at its foot, a stroke printed high and a god, and ·f. ḥry-ib 'who is in the midst of' is the face ḥr and the heart ib, each with its stroke, as in the hymn to Osiris. ṯꜣfy is a small bird with a raised wing (coded G47, approximate), the sign ṯꜣ, the viper f and two strokes y, the dual ending, with two gods; before the bird the print has a small × (coded Z9), which is not read. Budge reads T'afi, 'the two Tchafi'; the pair is not named elsewhere in the papyrus so far, and the reading is not sure. 'His' points back to a god not named in the statement; the next part opens with the question on it.

glossary.mꜣꜣ-m-grḥ-in-n-f-m-hrw: mꜣꜣ-m-grḥ-in-n-f-m-hrw — Maa-em-gereh-in-nef-em-heru, 'He who sees by night and brings by day' (?), one of the seven spirits (god's name; reading doubtful; Budge: Maa-em-ḳerḥ-àn-nef-em-hru)
glossary.ḥry: ḥry — upper, who/which is above, upon (nisba of ḥr)
glossary.irwd: irwd — a building or place (?), not identified (noun; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: àruṭ, 'hall')
glossary.nḏ: nḏ — to protect, guard (verb) · in the compound nḏ-ḥr 'to protect, take care of' (verb; with ḥr 'face')
glossary.itf: itf — father (noun m.; plural itw 'fathers, forefathers')
glossary.pf: pf — that (masculine demonstrative, after its noun; fem. tf)
glossary.sḏm·tw·f: sḏm·tw·f — the tw of the sḏm·tw·f, the passive or impersonal form ("one …", "… is done") (verb form; written after the verb, before its suffix)
glossary.wḏ: wḏ — to command, decree, ordain (verb) · also wḏt 'command, decree' (noun f., from the verb) · also wḏ 'command, decree' (noun m.)
glossary.ink: ink — I (1st person singular independent pronoun; ink N "I am N")
glossary.ḥry-ib: ḥry-ib — middle, midst (noun; lit. "what is upon the heart"; m ḥry-ib "in the midst of") · also the inside, inner parts (of the body) · also who is in the midst of, who dwells in (nisba epithet after a noun or name; nṯr ꜥꜣ ḥry-ib ꜣbḏw 'the great god who dwells in Abydos')
glossary.ṯꜣfy: ṯꜣfy — the Two Tjafi (?), a pair of gods (dual name; reading uncertain; Budge: T'afi, 'the two Tchafi')
